# Enable the context-budget pre-push gate across all framework projects

## Problem statement

Every project that runs the installed pi framework should block a local `git push`
to `dev` when the pi-session startup context surface regresses beyond a
project-appropriate budget. The original rollout plan (2026-08-10) listed six
non-SorraAgents projects, but the framework tooling has since landed and the
project landscape has changed; this intake refreshes the brief to the actual
2026-09-27 state and pins the remaining work.

## Users

- **Framework maintainers** — want a context regression caught locally, before
  it reaches `dev`.
- **Project developers** (e.g. AI_Hell contributors) — should not have to
  remember to run the gate manually.

Example user stories:

- As a framework maintainer, I want every framework project to run the
  context-budget gate on push, so that a skills/AGENTS.md regression cannot
  silently raise session cost across projects.
- As an AI_Hell developer, I want the same pre-push protection as SorraAgents,
  so that my project's startup context does not drift unnoticed.

## Current state (re-verified 2026-10-14; originally verified 2026-09-27)

The original brief's premises are **stale**. The following already landed
(SorraAgents git history):

| Commit | Item | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `6fbc38cf` | SA-0MT1WMPKZ008DL7S | global-symlink fallback for `measure_context.py` in `.githooks/pre-push` |
| `eca4ae60` | SA-0MT1WNWP2007KU7U / SA-0MT1WO815009KXUC | `--generate-thresholds` / `--write-thresholds` in `measure_context.py` |
| `6052e69c` | SA-0MT1WTF170058NJ7 / SA-0MT1WUEIT006U1HC | `install_pi.sh` wires the v2 hook + `core.hooksPath` |
| `3ca016bd` | SA-0MT1WURSU009NAXS | rollout docs in `docs/dev/context-budget.md` |
| `ddc6f6f5` | SA-0MT1WOWAO000T2P1 | hook passes `--repo-root` (global-symlink correctness) |

Project wiring (verified directly):

| Project | hook | `core.hooksPath` | thresholds | In scope? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SorraAgents | v3 (gate + sync + test gate) | `.git/hooks` | yes (15,473 B) | canonical |
| ContextHub | v2 | `.githooks` | yes (1,894 B) | yes |
| dev-scripts | v2 | `.githooks` | yes (371 B) | yes |
| llm-manager | v2 | `.githooks` | yes (967 B) | yes |
| open_source_llm | v2 | `.githooks` | yes (2,048 B) | yes |
| Tableau-Card-Engine | v2 | `.githooks` | yes (46,807 B) | yes |
| AI_Hell | **v1 (sync only)** | **unset** | **none** (project AGENTS.md = 24,044 B) | **yes — ungated** |
| ampa | v1 (sync only) | unset | none | **no — retired 2026-08-20**; checkout removed from disk 2026-10-14 |

Notes:

- `docs/dev/context-budget.md` (§ Rollout to all framework projects) states
  ampa was retired on 2026-08-20 and is out of scope. On 2026-10-14 its
  checkout was moved off disk (`~/.trash/ampa-2026-10-14`); git history is
  intact on `origin` and the local worklog held 0 items, so nothing unique was
  lost. ampa's gate wiring is therefore no longer relevant work.
- The brief's claim that "the global `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` is symlinked to all
  projects" is inaccurate: `install_pi.sh` symlinks it to
  `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` (machine-global), not into each repo. Consequently
  `measure_context.py` reports `global_agents = 0` and (mostly)
  `skills_prose = 0` in non-SorraAgents repos; each project's gate protects its
  **repo-local** surface, and the global surface is gated by SorraAgents itself.
- AI_Hell is an active framework project (last commit 2026-09-27) with a v1
  hook and no thresholds — a genuine remaining gap under the item title
  "across all framework projects".

## Target outcome

Every in-scope framework project's push to `dev` runs the context-budget gate
with project-appropriate committed thresholds. The only remaining project is
AI_Hell; the rollout is otherwise complete and should be verified end-to-end
before this item is closed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: v2 pre-push hook resolves `measure_context.py` from the local repo path
  when present, else the installed global symlink
  (`~/.pi/agent/skills/context-audit/scripts/measure_context.py`), and stays
  fail-open only when the framework is absent entirely. *(met — `tests/test_pre_push_hook_fallback.py`)*
- AC2: A repeatable per-project baseline flow emits a committed thresholds file
  (`docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json`) for the project.
  *(met — `measure_context.py --write-thresholds`; `tests/test_measure_context.py`)*
- AC3: The v2 hook + gate + `core.hooksPath` are installed in **every in-scope**
  framework project. *(partial — 5 of 5 listed projects done; **AI_Hell
  outstanding**; ampa retired/out of scope)*
- AC4: Worklog sync behaviour is preserved in every project (no v1→v2
  regression). *(met for wired projects — v2 hook contains the sync block)*
- AC5: `scripts/install_pi.sh` propagates the hook/global tooling so future
  projects get the gate automatically, and docs describe the mechanism.
  *(met — `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py`; `docs/dev/context-budget.md`)*
- AC6: End-to-end verification: a simulated push in at least one real
  non-SorraAgents framework project fires the gate (blocks an over-budget
  surface, passes a within-budget one). *(unmet — only temp-repo unit tests
  exist; no recorded real-project verification)*
- AC7: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
  code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
  *(pending — refresh rollout table with AI_Hell and the corrected
  global/local measurement note)*
- AC8: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (pytest + Node),
  including `tests/test_context_budget_gate.py`,
  `tests/test_pre_push_hook_fallback.py`, and
  `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py`. *(pending confirmation)*

## Constraints

- ampa is out of scope (retired 2026-08-20 per `docs/dev/context-budget.md`;
  checkout removed from disk 2026-10-14).
- The gate must remain fail-open when the framework/tooling is absent (old
  worktrees, machines without pi).
- `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` is the repo-level wiring mechanism
  (SorraAgents itself uses `.git/hooks`; do not change that without reason).
- Thresholds are generated from a project's own measurement; no shared global
  threshold value.
- Do not add CI/CD pipeline tests.

## Desired change

1. Run `scripts/install_pi.sh` (or the hook-wiring block) in AI_Hell to install
   the v2 `.githooks/pre-push` hook and set `core.hooksPath=.githooks`.
2. Generate and commit AI_Hell's own
   `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` from its measurement
   (`--write-thresholds`).
3. Update `docs/dev/context-budget.md`'s rollout table/notes to include AI_Hell
   and correct the global-vs-local measurement statement.
4. Add or record an end-to-end simulated-push verification for one real
   non-SorraAgents project (AI_Hell is the natural candidate).
5. Confirm the SorraAgents full suite is green.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `/home/rgardler/projects/AI_Hell/.githooks/pre-push` — replace v1 with v2
  (worklog sync + context-budget gate + branch policy).
- `/home/rgardler/projects/AI_Hell/docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` —
  new, generated from AI_Hell's measurement (project_agents ≈ 24,044 B).
- `/home/rgardler/projects/AI_Hell/.git/config` — set `core.hooksPath=.githooks`.
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — already wires hooks; verify it runs cleanly in
  AI_Hell (no code change expected).
- `docs/dev/context-budget.md` — rollout table + global/local measurement note.
- `tests/test_context_budget_gate.py`, `tests/test_pre_push_hook_fallback.py`,
  `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py` — regression coverage.

## Related work

- F6 (SA-0MSLK7XNZ00366YY) — gate tooling + SorraAgents thresholds (done).
- SA-0MSN2LIOQ004TON1 — activates the gate in SorraAgents' active hooks.
- SA-0MT1WMPKZ008DL7S — global fallback in the hook.
- SA-0MT1WNWP2007KU7U / SA-0MT1WO815009KXUC — threshold generation tooling.
- SA-0MT1WTF170058NJ7 / SA-0MT1WUEIT006U1HC — `install_pi.sh` hook wiring.
- SA-0MT1WURSU009NAXS — rollout documentation.
- SA-0MT1WOWAO000T2P1 — `--repo-root` fix for global-symlink correctness.
- Automated report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-SA-0MSN2ULOF007JJ35.md`.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Resolved (2026-10-14):** ampa is out of scope (retired per
  `docs/dev/context-budget.md`) and its checkout has been removed from disk.
  No ampa wiring remains.
- **Assumption:** AI_Hell is in scope because the item title says "all framework
  projects" and AI_Hell is an active project with `AGENTS.md` and a v1 worklog
  hook; it was simply absent from the 2026-08-10 enumeration.
- **Risk (scope creep):** re-baselining the five already-wired projects is not
  required; only AI_Hell needs wiring. Record any further projects as
  discovered-from items rather than expanding this brief.
- **Risk:** per-project gates report `global_agents = 0` because the global
  file is not repo-local. Document this so the gate is not mistaken for
  covering the global surface in those repos.
- **Risk (verification gap):** without a real-project simulated push, AC3/AC6
  rely on unit tests only. Close with an actual push rehearsal.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1:** The item's premise is stale — the tooling and five of the six listed
  projects are already wired, and `docs/dev/context-budget.md` says ampa was
  retired 2026-08-20. How should this item be scoped now? Options: **(A)** close
  as satisfied after an end-to-end verification; **(B)** narrow it to wiring the
  remaining ungated active framework project (AI_Hell) plus verification;
  **(C)** retain the original six-project scope.
  **Answer (producer, 2026-10-14, interactive reply):** **B** — narrow the item
  to wiring AI_Hell and end-to-end verification. **Agent recommended:** B.

- **Q2:** Is **AI_Hell** in scope? It is an active framework project
  (`AGENTS.md` + v1 worklog pre-push, `core.hooksPath` unset, no thresholds) but
  was not in the original six-project enumeration (ContextHub, dev-scripts,
  llm-manager, open_source_llm, Tableau-Card-Engine, ampa).
  **Answer (producer, 2026-10-14, interactive reply):** **Yes.**
  **Agent recommended:** Yes.

- **Q3:** Confirm **ampa** remains out of scope. Its checkout still carries the
  v1 hook (`core.hooksPath` unset, no thresholds) but the rollout docs mark it
  retired as of 2026-08-20.
  **Answer (producer, 2026-10-14, interactive reply):** **Yes** — and ampa
  should be removed from disk. **Action:** checkout moved to
  `~/.trash/ampa-2026-10-14` (git history intact on `origin`; local worklog
  empty), so no ampa wiring remains. **Agent recommended:** Yes.

# Replace scan.py find-workitem with native wl CLI lookup in audit prompts

## Problem statement

The audit SCANNING blocks and docs currently recommend
`scan.py find-workitem <id>` for worklog lookups (wired in by
SA-0MSBR0SRK0035HB1; guidance refined by SA-0MSOIS36N0024ORI).
`scan.py find-workitem` wraps `wl search <id> --json` plus an exact-id
post-filter. Once the wl CLI gains tolerant ID resolution (the ContextHub
feature below), audit agents should use native wl commands for worklog
lookups and `scan.py find-workitem` can be retired.

## Blocked by

- **WL-0MSOMI4GQ009WL8E** — "Add tolerant work-item ID resolution to `wl show`
  (exact-first, unique substring fallback, ambiguity error) for agent tool
  use" — feature request in the **ContextHub** repository
  (`/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub`), created 2026-08-11.

This item MUST NOT start until that feature lands in the installed wl CLI
(the exact-match `wl show` today cannot resolve partial/truncated IDs, which
is why the scan.py wrapper exists). Cross-project dependency — recorded here
as a blocker; not a `wl dep` edge (different worklog DBs).

## Substring-matching guidance (researched — use ONLY the optimal command)

The canonical substring-matching primitive is **`wl list <term> --json`**:
case-insensitive substring match over id/title/description, JSON mode returns
all matches, supports `-n/--number` and filters (see `src/commands/list.ts`
in ContextHub).

`wl search <keywords> --json` is full-text search (FTS, token/prefix-based) —
**not** a substring matcher — and must NOT be presented as one.

Exact / unique-ID resolution: **`wl show <id> --json`** (tolerant once
WL-0MSOMI4GQ009WL8E lands; `scan.py find-workitem <id>` interim).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. All SCANNING blocks in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`
   (`_PHASE1_SCANNING_BLOCK`, phase2_child, phase2_batch, phase2_deep) direct
   worklog lookups to native wl commands only:
   - substring matching: `wl list <term> --json`
   - exact/unique-ID resolution: `wl show <id> --json`
2. The dual recommendation "`wl search <keywords> --json` or
   `wl list <term> --json` for substring matching" (introduced by
   SA-0MSOIS36N0024ORI) is corrected to the single optimal command
   **`wl list <term> --json`** everywhere it appears (audit_runner.py +
   docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md), per the research note above.
3. `scan.py find-workitem` is removed (subcommand, its tests, and references
   in audit-grep-scan-patterns.md) OR deprecated with a clear notice — the
   decision is documented in a comment; `scan.py search-code` and
   `scan.py list-files` remain unchanged.
4. docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md and docs/dev/audit-grep-scan-patterns.md
   (incl. the P9 replacement recipe) updated to the native commands.
5. Full project test suite passes (canonical PATH with `~/.local/bin`).
6. Related docs (README, wiki/docs-site entries, code comments, scan.py
   module docstring) updated; no stale `scan.py find-workitem` guidance
   remains.

## Out of scope

- No changes to `scan.py search-code` / `list-files` (bounded code search).
- No changes to the wl CLI itself — tracked in ContextHub WL-0MSOMI4GQ009WL8E.
- No changes to audit verdict semantics or prompt structure beyond the
  worklog-lookup guidance lines.

## Related work

- SA-0MSOIS36N0024ORI — removed stale `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` grep
  guidance from audit prompts (completed, this item's precursor).
- SA-0MSBR0SRK0035HB1 — wired scan.py guidance into audit prompts (the
  guidance this item replaces).
- SA-0MSAEJCP7002LTIM / SA-0MSBSOAEM0078LAO — scan hygiene parents.
data.title: Replace scan.py find-workitem with native wl CLI lookup in audit prompts (blocked by ContextHub WL-0MSOMI4GQ009WL8E)

# Tune audit queue timeout / concurrency ceiling to eliminate residual bounded-queue saturation

## Problem statement

The bounded priority queue (SA-0MTG5RYH8005RQNM) eliminated fail-fast audit
re-queueing (27 → 0), but under peak-day traffic **14 items still exhausted the
bounded wait and returned a `bounded-queue saturation` verdict** (latest live
metrics: 3 residual, down from 14 at evaluation time). Per
`docs/dev/downtime-idle-gate-evaluation.md`, this is a **capacity/timeout
problem — not an idle-gate problem**: the configured concurrency ceilings are
lower than the host's real audit-slot capacity, so peak bursts queue beyond
what the timeout bound permits.

## Users

- **Operators** running the herdr downtime dispatcher: they expect audits to
  complete with real verdicts even during peak multi-agent traffic, not return
  an `unmet` "concurrency limit reached" verdict after a full wait.
- **Agent sessions** whose audits time out under saturation: today they burn a
  full bounded wait (90–115 s) and either retry later or leave items stuck in
  `in_review`.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Right-sized ceilings:** `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` and/or
   `AUDIT_MAX_HOST_AUDITS` defaults are raised to the host's real audit-slot
   capacity, *measured empirically* via the existing F7 harness
   (`skill/shared/validate_fanout.py` — the largest ceiling that keeps load
   < 16 on the 16-core host with no swap growth), informed by the 3-slot local
   LLM proxy pool.

2. **Timeout stays bash-window-safe:** `AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT` remains bounded
   (≈90–115 s) inside the parent bash-tool execution window (~120 s), so the
   SA-0MSGEAZMC009LHKL mid-wait-kill failure mode is not reintroduced.

3. **Zero residual saturation:** with N ≥ 3 concurrent audits against a busy
   host, **zero** `bounded-queue saturation` (or `host-wide saturation`)
   `unmet` verdicts are produced — all audits persist **real** verdicts
   (verification mirrors SA-0MTG5RYH8005RQNM AC1).

4. **No regression:** existing concurrency/queue tests keep passing —
   `test_audit_runner_concurrency.py`, `test_audit_queue_integration.py`,
   `test_audit_slot_lock_contention.py` — including the "timeout ≥ 0.1s < 5s
   bounded wait" behaviour and priority-ordering assertions; no test relies on
   the old default values being treated as constants.

5. **Documentation updated:** `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (fix the
   documented ceiling default — prose currently claims 2 while
   `process_semaphore.py` default is 5), `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`
   (host-cap defaults), and the follow-up status in
   `docs/dev/downtime-idle-gate-evaluation.md`.

6. **Full suite green:** the full project test suite passes with the changes
   (build → test → commit order per AGENTS.md).

## Constraints

- **Do NOT relax the herdr idle gate** (rejected in SA-0MTG5UPBR0028K50); no
  ContextHub dispatcher change is in scope.
- Keep priority ordering (critical > high > medium > low; FIFO within tier)
  and the bounded-wait semantics of the shared priority queue unchanged.
- `AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT` must not exceed the parent bash-tool execution timeout
  (~120 s) unless the dispatch model changes — decoupling the wait from the
  bash-tool window is **out of scope**.
- The host's real capacity is bounded by the local LLM proxy
  (`session_slot_pool_size: 3` default) plus CPU/RAM headroom — the empirical
  F7 measurement is the source of truth.

## Existing state

| Knob | Default | Where | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT` | 90.0 s | `audit_runner.py:289-290` | Bounded queue+slot wait; 90s chosen to stay inside bash-tool ~120s window (SA-0MSGEAZMC009LHKL) |
| `AUDIT_LOCK_TIMEOUT` | 0.0 s | `audit_runner.py` | Per-attempt fail-fast inside the admission poll; total wait governed by queue timeout |
| `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY` (`DEFAULT_MAX_WORKERS`) | 5 | `process_semaphore.py:75-76` | `_audit_semaphore_max_workers` precedence: CLI > env > 5 |
| `AUDIT_MAX_HOST_AUDITS` | 3 | `audit_runner.py:250-251` | Host-wide ingress cap (`audit-host` semaphore) |
| `AUDIT_HOST_LOCK_TIMEOUT` | 90.0 s | `audit_runner.py:252-253` | Bounded wait for host ingress slot |
| Queue `max_depth` | 50 | `queue.py:94` | `QUEUE_MAX_DEPTH` override |

- Latest live metrics (2026-10-13): 771 admissions; bounded-queue saturation
  **3**; host-wide saturation 0; legacy fail-fast 0; max observed wait 599.8 s
  (historical, from a higher-override period).
- No deployment/pi/herdr env overrides for these knobs — **code defaults
  currently govern every project**. The herdr dispatcher sets only
  `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=1`.

## Desired change

Raise the audit concurrency ceilings to the **empirically measured** host
capacity (via `validate_fanout.py`, respecting the 3-slot proxy pool), keep
`AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT` bounded inside the bash-tool window, and update the
defaults + documentation so peak bursts drain through the queue instead of
timing out. Verify with N ≥ 3 concurrent audits against a busy host with zero
concurrency-limit `unmet` verdicts.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — ceiling/timeout defaults
  (`AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT`, `AUDIT_MAX_HOST_AUDITS_DEFAULT`,
  `AUDIT_HOST_LOCK_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT`), `_audit_queue_timeout()`,
  `_acquire_audit_slot()`, `_acquire_host_audit_slot()` (see ~line 3402,
  12468-12554)
- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` — `DEFAULT_MAX_WORKERS` /
  `ENV_MAX_WORKERS` (`AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY`) ceiling
- `skill/shared/validate_fanout.py` — F7 load-validation harness for
  empirical capacity measurement (mock pi, throwaway worklog)
- `skill/shared/audit_gate_metrics.py` — read-only metrics collector for
  verification (reports bounded-queue saturation counts)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_concurrency.py` — ceiling/timeout
  default tests (`test_default_ceiling_documented`,
  `test_default_queue_timeout_is_bounded_not_fail_fast`)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_queue_integration.py` — queue-wait and
  priority-ordering tests
- `skill/shared/tests/test_audit_slot_lock_contention.py` — lock-contention
  timeout tests
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — concurrency docs (fix stated default)
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` — host-cap documentation
- `docs/dev/downtime-idle-gate-evaluation.md` — evaluation + follow-up status

## Related work

- **SA-0MTG5UPBR0028K50** (done) — idle-gate evaluation; recommended this
  follow-up (`discovered-from`); do not relax the herdr idle gate.
- **SA-0MTG5RYH8005RQNM** (done) — bounded priority queue integration; AC1
  north-star "zero concurrency-limit unmet verdicts" — this item's target.
- **SA-0MTG5N7BN003D95L** (done) — shared bounded priority queue module.
- **SA-0MTG5TP5Z008QBL5** (done) — batch drain mode.
- **SA-0MUV4C6RZ006GN5Z / SA-0MV0J0XXR008ZE6E** (done) — directory-lock
  timeout bounds.
- **SA-0MU7FD0YF0065EG9** (done) — stale queue-ticket saturation.
- **SA-0MU32T8SH001R8MZ** (done) — R4: no saturation abort of Phase 1 parent.
- **SA-0MSAEKOQE009TEB4** (done) — fan-out investigation (parent of F7).
- **SA-0MTG0Y34T007ZHPF** — parent: multi-agent blocking on audits.
- **SA-0MSGEAZMC009LHKL** — prior art: 300s default killed audits mid-wait
  (origin of the bash-window constraint).
- **SA-0MSAWFTZX003T042** (done) — audit completion status semantics.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Raising ceilings raises concurrent suite runners** — mitigated by the
  F7-measured ceiling (load < 16, no swap growth) and the existing host-wide
  `audit-host` ingress cap; do not exceed measured capacity.
- **Cheap-proxy serialization** (01:00–10:00) already forces
  `AUDIT_MAX_CONCURRENCY=1` in some windows — tuning must not fight that
  gate; verify in both modes.
- **Scope-creep risk:** decoupling the queue wait from the bash-tool window,
  relaxing the idle gate, or re-architecting dispatch is explicitly **out of
  scope**; record as linked follow-ups if discovered.
- **Assumption:** code-default changes are the correct mechanism since no
  deployment override exists today (operator confirmed).
- **Assumption:** the empirical F7 result, informed by the 3-slot proxy pool,
  is the definition of "the host's real audit slot capacity" (operator
  confirmed).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Lever priority — raise concurrency ceilings vs raise timeout vs both?"
  — Answer (operator): "As you recommend" → **Option A: raise the concurrency
  ceilings and keep `AUDIT_QUEUE_TIMEOUT` bounded (~90–115 s) inside the
  bash-tool window.** Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "Where the tuning lives — code defaults vs deployment env vs both?"
  — Answer (operator): "As you recommend" → **Option A: change the code
  defaults** (single source of truth; no deployment override exists).
  Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Capacity target definition — fixed number vs empirical F7 vs match
  proxy pool?" — Answer (operator): "As you recommend" → **Option B: measure
  empirically with `validate_fanout.py` (load < 16, no swap growth), informed
  by the 3-slot proxy pool.** Source: interactive reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MQFXVJAZ004A29L** – wl close should recursively close children if in-review and audit OK (completed)
- **SA-0MUD8SBS2001P6G2** – Reproduce order-pollution deterministically (completed)
- **SA-0MUIUTJJS008W06Y** – plan-approval-gate skips checkpoint for t-shirt effort and Severe risk (open)

data.description:
# Ship skill: release flow leaves derived version files stale — regenerate post-bump

## Headline

The ship skill's release flow bumps `package.json` but never regenerates consumer
repos' auto-generated version files (e.g. ContextHub `src/version.ts`), so a
release can ship with a stale derived version until the next build runs —
breaking version-parity tests. Fix: the release flow runs the repo's `npm run build`
after the bump (non-fatally) and commits the regenerated tracked files.

## Problem statement

The ship release flow (`merge-dev-to-main.sh` → `bump-version.js`) increments the
version in **`package.json` only**. Consumer repositories that derive a
CLI/runtime version from `package.json` via a build step (e.g. ContextHub's
auto-generated `src/version.ts`, written by `scripts/generate-version.cjs` during
`npm run build`) are left with a **stale derived version** until the next build
runs, so version-parity assertions fail right after a release.

## Users

- **Consumer repo maintainers** (e.g. ContextHub) whose repo derives a CLI/runtime
  version from `package.json` and tracks the derived file (and whose tests assert
  version parity).
  - *User story:* "As a maintainer of a consumer CLI repo, I want the ship release
    to regenerate my derived version file so that my version-parity tests are green
    immediately after a release, without me manually running `npm run build`."
- **Release operators** running `/skill:ship release` — want the release to never
  leave downstream tests broken by stale versions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] After `bump-version.js` bumps `package.json` in `merge-dev-to-main.sh` (real
  release mode), the release flow runs the repo's `npm run build` when a `build`
  script exists, and commits the regenerated **tracked** files — so a consumer
  repo's derived version file (e.g. ContextHub `src/version.ts`) matches the bumped
  `package.json` by the time the release completes. Verified by a green version-parity
  test on a consumer repo, or an equivalent unit test of the ship flow using a fixture
  repo.
- [ ] A failing regeneration step does **not** abort the release: a `Warning:`
  message is logged and the release continues, mirroring the CHANGELOG step's
  non-fatal behaviour. Verified by a unit/script test with a failing build script.
- [ ] The mechanism and its trigger are documented: `skill/ship/SKILL.md` and
  `docs/dev/release-process.md` describe that a post-bump, pre-tag build
  regeneration runs on the final merged tree when `scripts.build` exists and is
  non-fatal.
- [ ] A regression test for the ship flow exists (unit test of the regeneration
  step with an injected build command / fixture repo), covering both success and
  failure paths.
- [ ] Existing ship tests pass and the full SorraAgents test suite passes with the
  new changes.

## Constraints

- **Non-fatal regeneration:** a failed or slow build must never block the release
  (operator-confirmed choice); the release path and exit codes stay unchanged.
- **Tracked files only:** commit regenerated files via `git add -u` (or equivalent)
  so build droppings (e.g. `dist/`, new untracked artefacts) are not staged.
- **Trigger sparingly:** only run when a `build` script exists in `package.json`;
  no new mandatory dependencies, no opt-in flags required.
- **Dry-run parity:** `--dry-run` reports the would-be regeneration (like the other
  dry-run echoes) and performs no build/commit.
- Repos that do **not** track their derived version file are out of scope (the
  prerequisite for this fix is that the derived file is committed, as in ContextHub).

## Existing state

- `bump-version.js` reads/writes `package.json` only; the bumped version is
  committed by `merge-dev-to-main.sh` ("Bump version to vX") before merging `dev`.
- The same script already runs a post-bump **non-fatal** regeneration precedent for
  `CHANGELOG.md` (`generate-changelog.js`; `Warning: … continuing with release`),
  which this change mirrors.
- ContextHub tracks `src/version.ts` (`WORKLOG_VERSION`), regenerated by
  `scripts/generate-version.cjs` inside `npm run build`; its parity guard
  `tests/unit/version-parity.test.ts` (commit cf8c09a7) fails fast on drift.
- SorraAgents itself has a no-op `build` script, so this repo is unaffected; the
  step must remain harmless for repos with no real build.

## Desired change

In `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh`, after the dev merge (final
tree) and before tagging, run the repo's `npm run build` when `scripts.build`
exists, then stage regenerated tracked files and commit them (e.g. "Regenerate
derived version files for vX"). On build failure, log a warning and continue. Mirror
the CHANGELOG handling for dry-run output. Optionally extract the step into a small
testable Node helper (pattern: `generate-changelog.js` + its test) selected by the
plan step.

## Key Files:

- `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` — add post-merge build + commit step (primary change).
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-version.js` — unchanged in the thin case; the derivation trigger may be extracted into a small sibling helper if a unit-test boundary is required.
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — document the new step and trigger.
- `docs/dev/release-process.md` — document the new step and trigger (version-bump section, ~line 156).
- New unit test for the regeneration step (fixture repo / injected build command), pattern: `skill/ship/tests/test_generate_changelog_focus.mjs`.

## Related work

- WL-0MV7GV4XW0073FCD — ContextHub triage item for the observed drift (version-parity test failure); consumer-side guard cf8c09a7.
- SA-0MRC71KCR009Y7RL — *Generate CHANGELOG.md during ship release process* (completed) — the post-bump non-fatal regeneration precedent.
- SA-0MPYO85WW006CXPL — *Add version numbering to ship skill for releases* (completed) — introduced the bump step.
- SA-0MRB2FB5X008X4MM, SA-0MQI6MDUP001S8NL — bump-version.js install-path fixes (completed).

### Related work (automated report)

_run: `find_related.py --work-item-id SA-0MV7WAUHZ009UWY2` (full report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-SA-0MV7WAUHZ009UWY2.md`)_

Related work items (all completed; context for ship-skill/test-runner behaviour, none conflicting):

- **SA-0MSP7RGX3005HMD0** – *Ship skill scripts unreachable from documented paths* — relevant precedent for changing ship-skill scripts/docs in lockstep.
- **SA-0MSF8KNE3003JDVD** – *Fix node --test directory invocation in test skill runner* — relevant to how the new ship-flow regression test is added under `skill/ship/tests/`.
- **SA-0MS4A7A4Y000L9ED** – *Update cross-references, clean up old files, and verify tests pass* — the cross-reference/documentation-sync pattern.

Repo-file matches returned were generic keyword collisions (e.g. `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`) and are excluded as noise.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Build slowness/failure:** a full build may take minutes or fail for reasons
  unrelated to version derivation — mitigated by non-fatal failure semantics;
  slowness only affects real releases of build-bearing repos.
- **`git add -u` scope:** only already-tracked files are staged; a derived file
  that is newly generated (untracked/gitignored) is not captured — recorded as an
  assumption, not in scope.
- **Commit noise:** regenerated generated-source (e.g. `src/version.ts`) becomes part
  of the release commit; acceptable and desired for parity, and limited to tracked
  files.
- **Scope-creep risk:** generalising to arbitrary derived artefacts or
  multi-repo/CI regeneration is out of scope; record such opportunities as linked
  work items rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Mechanism — Option A (active regeneration) vs Option B (documentation only)
  vs Hybrid?" — Answer (operator): "A — active regeneration: after bump-version.js
  commits the new package.json version, the release flow runs the repo's
  `npm run build` when a `build` script exists, then commits the regenerated tracked
  files." Source: interactive reply (intake session).
- Q2: "If active regeneration is chosen — if the post-bump build fails, abort the
  release or warn and continue?" — Answer (operator): "B — warn and continue,
  mirroring the CHANGELOG step's non-fatal behaviour." Source: interactive reply
  (intake session). Prior: none. Research: the existing CHANGELOG generation step
  (`Warning: CHANGELOG.md generation failed (continuing with release)`) provides the
  established non-fatal pattern in the same script.
data.title: Ship skill: bump-version.js leaves derived version files stale (drift breaks consumer CLI version checks)

data.description:
Discovered from SA-0MSN2ULOF007JJ35 (context-budget gate rollout).

## Problem

`scripts/install_pi.sh` copies the *current* SorraAgents `.githooks/pre-push` (header `worklog:pre-push-hook:v3`) into a project when that project has no `.githooks/pre-push`. The v3 hook includes a **SorraAgents-only full-suite test gate** that hard-fails `exit 1` when the repo-local runner `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` is absent:

```
ERROR: /tmp/.../skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py not found — cannot run the full-suite gate for a dev/main push.
```

No sibling framework project ships `skill/` (all use the installed global skill symlinks), so a **freshly wired non-SorraAgents project would have every push to `dev` blocked** after running install_pi.sh. This contradicts the script's own comment ("Install the v2 pre-push hook") and the documented framework v2 hook contract (`docs/dev/context-budget.md`, "worklog sync + context-budget gate + branch policy" — no test gate).

Existing sibling projects (ContextHub, dev-scripts, llm-manager, open_source_llm, Tableau-Card-Engine) predate the v3 test gate and therefore still ship the safe v2 hook. AI_Hell was wired manually with v2 in SA-0MSN2ULOF007JJ35 precisely to avoid this.

## Evidence

```bash
# real SorraAgents v3 hook run as a non-SorraAgents project's pre-push, simulated dev push
cd /tmp/fresh-project && cp .../SorraAgents/.githooks/pre-push .githooks-pre-push
printf 'refs/heads/dev 0000 refs/heads/dev 1111
' | \
  WORKLOG_SKIP_PRE_PUSH=1 BRANCH_POLICY_SKIP=1 CONTEXT_BUDGET_SKIP=1 sh .githooks-pre-push
# → exit 1: run_tests.py not found
```

## Desired change

Make install_pi.sh install a framework-safe hook outside the canonical source repo — e.g. ship a dedicated v2 template (context-budget gate + worklog sync + branch policy, minus the SorraAgents-only test gate) and copy that, or make the v3 test gate fail-open when the repo-local runner is absent. Add a test asserting a freshly wired non-SorraAgents project's dev push is not blocked by a missing local test runner.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A project wired by install_pi.sh with no repo-local `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` does not have its `dev`/`main` pushes blocked by the full-suite test gate.
- AC2: The context-budget gate + worklog sync + branch policy remain present in the installed hook.
- AC3: Regression test covers the fresh-project install path.
- AC4: `docs/dev/context-budget.md` and install_pi.sh comments accurately describe which hook is installed where.

## Related

- discovered-from:SA-0MSN2ULOF007JJ35
